working_title: Scotland's Aberdeenshire Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Cruden Bay, Royal Aberdeen and Beyond
angle: Aberdeenshire is the stretch of Scottish links golf that most UK visitors skip because they anchor trips around St Andrews to the south or Royal Dornoch to the north. This guide makes the case for a dedicated two-to-three day circuit along the North Sea coast, covering the headline names and a handful of affordable supporting acts, with honest practical information on access, green fees, and how to sequence the trip.
research_notes:
- Aberdeenshire's North Sea coastline has been described as having 'some of the finest seaside courses anywhere on the planet, many of which remain refreshingly free from the crowds' (top100golfcourses.com, March 2026 update)
- Key courses in the circuit: Royal Aberdeen (Balgownie), Murcar Links, Cruden Bay, Trump International (Old Course + New Course opened July 2025), Royal Tarlair, Fraserburgh, Peterhead Craigewan, Newburgh-on-Ythan, Stonehaven
- Cruden Bay: 23 miles north of Aberdeen on the A90/A975; Old Tom Morris laid out the original course in 1899, Tom Simpson redesigned in 1926; course plays through the dunes rather than around them, with fairways disappearing over ridges and greens in natural amphitheatres; visitors welcome 7 days a week, weekends limited to afternoons; booking via crudenbaygolfclub.co.uk up to 12 months ahead
- Cruden Bay 2026 green fees (per one source): approx. £205 weekday / £220 weekend peak season, ~£140 shoulder, ~£110 winter (note: sources give slightly varying figures — use ranges, not single hard numbers, and flag visitors should check directly)
- Royal Aberdeen (Balgownie): traditional out-and-back links on the North Sea shore; founded 1780 as Society of Golfers at Aberdeen; course designed by Simpson Brothers, later re-bunkered and lengthened by James Braid
- Murcar Links: established 1909; defined by natural dunes, gorse, heather, elevated tees and sea views; frequently ranked among Scotland's top courses
- Trump International: Old Course (Martin Hawtree, 2012 design, 7,428 yards across the Menie Estate); New Course opened July 2025 — named World's Best Golf Course 2025 by World Golf Awards; hosting DP World Tour's Scottish Championship from 2025
- Royal Tarlair (Macduff): described as a long drive from Aberdeen (~55 mins) but the 13th hole is a notable draw; green fee around £25 (budget option)
- Fraserburgh GC: founded 1777, present course opened 1891, redesigned by James Braid 1922 — one of Scotland's oldest clubs
- Peterhead Craigewan Links: described informally as a 'hidden gem' on the coast
- Aberdeen Airport: 7 miles northwest of city centre; car hire is the practical option for combining multiple courses; Royal Aberdeen is ~20 minutes from the airport
- Travel from Edinburgh: A90 to Aberdeen ~2.5 hours; Cruden Bay a further 35 minutes north; train to Aberdeen also ~2.5 hours from Edinburgh but car hire then essential
- Aberdeen city base works well for Royal Aberdeen, Murcar, and Trump International; day trip to Cruden Bay is straightforward with a car
- Caddies can be arranged at Royal Aberdeen and Cruden Bay; recommended for first-time visitors unfamiliar with the blind shots and wind patterns
- Sensible itinerary structure: Day 1 Cruden Bay + explore Slains Castle; Day 2 Royal Aberdeen (morning) + Murcar or Trump (afternoon); Day 3 Royal Tarlair or Fraserburgh before driving south
- Weather/kit note: conditions can shift quickly on this coast; waterproofs, warm layers and a windproof jacket are essential
- The region can also be combined with whisky distillery visits and North Sea coastal walks for non-golfing companions
must_avoid:
